key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation with neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for robust HDPE joints by predicting temperatures, axial forces, material flow and weld defects.
method: Develop a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model across rotational speeds, welding speeds and bottom-preheating conditions.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force histories.
Use simulation and neural-network predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation showed good simulation agreement, ANN R² values of 0.91–0.99, and a peak plunge-force reduction from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N with 60 °C preheating.
watch_item: Predictive accuracy beyond the tested process conditions remains unestablished; new operating regimes require validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
